Grandpa had got very upset when his daughter, Ravi’s mother, insisted that he shouldn’t go out alone again. “I’ll have you know, Vidya, my dear,” he had told his daughter with a trace of the firmness that had been a natural part of his job as a lawyer, “that I’ve been looking after myself for the better part of my seventy-five years. After your mother died ten years ago, I took over her duties as well and have been cooking, shopping and keeping house too.

“I hope you’re not going to be as tiresome as your mother, Ravi. Treating me like a baby! Has she told you not to let me go out on my own? Told you to keep me a prisoner here, has she?” Grandpa looked suspicious at this thought. Ravi felt guilty for a moment, then quickly recovered to say loyally, “Of course not, Grandpa. Mamma would never treat you like a baby … or a prisoner.” “Good,” said Grandpa craftily, “then you’ll have no objection to my going out.”

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your cousin Ravi has brought his grandfather to live with his family. Write a letter of 100 words to Ravi suggesting three ways of looking after an elderly person at home so that he keeps his independence and does not feel bored.

markingPoints.description: Begins with a greeting and states the purpose of the letter in the opening lines
Gives three clear, practical ways of looking after an elderly person at home
Includes at least one way that protects the elderly person’s independence and self-respect
Organises the three ideas in a sensible order and links them smoothly
Uses accurate spelling, grammar and punctuation, and stays within 100 words

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Dear Ravi,

Now that your grandfather lives with you, here are three ideas.

First, let him help you at home. He has been cooking, shopping and keeping house all his life, so a small job will stop him feeling useless.

Second, play chess with him. He is very good at it and can tell you the moves his famous players made.

Third, do not decide everything for him. Ask what he wants to do, and warn him only when it is truly dangerous.

With love,
Your cousin

evidence: I took over her duties as well and have been cooking, shopping and keeping house too.
Grandpa played a great game of chess, very cool and cunning, and Ravi found that his own game had improved greatly ever since Grandpa had come to live with them.

Caring for the Elderly

Please note that each of us will be asked to write down one thing we learnt from an older person.

Teacher-in-charge

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Good morning, everyone. Today I want to talk about three things we can all do at home for the elderly.

First, listen to them. They may know the stories and the recipes of our own family.

Second, give them a small job in the house. A person who has cooked and shopped for a lifetime hates to sit idle.

Third, ask them before you decide for them. Treat them as grown-ups, not as babies.

If we do these three things every day, our homes will be happier places for all of us.

Thank you.

questions.stem: Trace the route taken by the old man after he leaves the flat, and state what happens to Ravi at each stop.

markingPoints.description: The children’s park is the first stop, where Ravi hides behind a bush trimmed in the shape of an elephant
At the tea stall Ravi hides behind a banyan tree and is surrounded by the vendors, while the old man eats tea, two bananas and an ice cream
The old man enters the barber shop and Ravi is thrown out of the Ladies’ Hairdressing Salon next door
At the bus stop the old man boards the first bus and Ravi jumps on after him
The yellow cap turns out to belong to a total stranger and not to his grandfather
Gives the stops in the order in which they happen, one clear step for each

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. Children’s park: he buys a paper-cone of peanuts and watches the children play. Ravi crouches behind a bush trimmed in the shape of an elephant, and a child’s mother accuses him of shooing her child.
2. Tea stall: Ravi hides behind a big banyan tree, but the vendors surround him and he concedes defeat. The old man has tea, two bananas and an ice cream.
3. Barber shop: he crosses the road and goes in. Ravi ducks into the shop next door and is thrown out of a Ladies’ Hairdressing Salon.
4. Bus stop: the old man boards the first bus. Ravi jumps on, sees the yellow cap taken off to reveal a full head of grey hair, and finds a total stranger wearing his grandfather’s cap.

evidence: bush trimmed in the shape of an elephant to avoid being seen.
Grandpa’s next stop was the tea stall, and this time Ravi took position behind a big banyan tree to watch him

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Ravi’s mother and Ravi both want to keep the old man safe, yet they look after him in very different ways. Compare how each of them behaves with him, and state what each one believes is best for him.

markingPoints.description: The mother locks up the tiny brick house and brings her father to live with them
She has his medicines given after lunch and forbids him to go out alone
She speaks to him in an over-loud tone, as though she were speaking to a child
She believes her father can no longer keep himself safe on his own
Ravi plays chess with him and lets him explain the moves, so the old man feels useful
Ravi follows him secretly at a safe distance and believes this keeps him safe without hurting his feelings

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Ravi’s mother: She locks up the brick house and brings her father to live with them. She has his medicines given after lunch, tells Ravi that the old man must not go out alone, and speaks to him in an over-loud tone, as though she were speaking to a child. She believes he can no longer keep himself safe.

Ravi: He plays chess with his grandfather and lets him explain the moves, so the old man feels useful and valued. Yet when the old man insists on going to the corner shop, Ravi hides his real intention, lies to him about his mother’s orders and follows him secretly at a safe distance. He believes this keeps his grandfather safe without hurting his feelings.

evidence: “Whatever happens, Ravi, you’re not to let Grandpa go out on his own. It’s too dangerous,” she instructed, adding details of medicines to be given to Grandpa after lunch.
Ravi found that his own game had improved greatly ever since Grandpa had come to live with them.
Ravi decided he would follow Grandpa secretly, at a safe distance, to make sure he came to no harm.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. After his wife died ten years ago he took over her duties too, cooking, shopping and keeping house, so he is sure he is capable.
2. He slipped and fell in the garden while pottering around and lay outside all night, with no one there to help him up.
3. His daughter became frightened, locked up the tiny brick house, brought him to live with them and told Ravi he must not go out alone.
4. The old man felt very upset at being stopped, and said he had looked after himself for seventy-five years.
5. Ravi knew his grandfather would feel hurt if he insisted on accompanying him.
6. So Ravi followed him secretly, at a safe distance, to make sure he came to no harm.
